A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same xKV research, and their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable. The original method, analyses, and evaluations can be matched despite extensive revision. Some internal inconsistencies in v2 limit individual numerical comparisons.

before.justification: V1 reports original RULER accuracy results, DeepSeek coding evaluations, cross-layer similarity analyses, and key/value compression ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original accuracy, multi-turn retrieval, latency, throughput, quantization, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The grouped cross-layer SVD remains, renamed Cross-Layer Factorization. V2 adds Selective Reconstruction, using query-dependent, head-specific token selection instead of reconstructing every prompt token, and introduces xK-SR with CPU-offloaded values. Section 3 and Appendix B describe a substantive extension of the inference procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates RULER and the LCC/RepoBench-P coding tasks. V2 adds broader LongBench coverage, including document QA, summarization, few-shot and synthetic tasks, plus five-turn NIAH evaluation. The multi-turn setting tests preservation of context across changing queries, extending the original task requirements.

E2.justification: V1 compares against MiniCache, Single SVD, and uncompressed models. V2 adds evaluated KIVI-2, PyramidKV, and SnapKV comparisons in RULER Table 1; Quest, ShadowKV, and value-compressed ShadowKV comparisons in Table 2; and StreamingLLM in LongBench Table 6.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a fixed 2K selected-token budget for its 64K RULER selection comparisons, A100 80GB efficiency tests across batch sizes at 60K/122K lengths, and prefill timing across 64K–256K contexts. Window-size and quantization experiments add controlled settings. These are new evaluation protocols; the PDFs do not establish why retained accuracy scores changed.

E4.justification: The original separate key/value ablation is retained as Figure 6. V2 adds window-size comparisons through eight layers across three variants, 3-bit/4-bit quantization compatibility tests, and CKA analyses for Llama-3.2-1B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Qwen3-4B. Multi-turn tests additionally probe robustness to changing queries.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The expanded results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial SR, multi-turn, LongBench, efficiency, and quantization results; Table 2 reports xKV-SR averaging 89.69 at 5.35× compression. Retained numerical entries also change: Llama-3.1-8B Single SVD at 64K and 8.4× compression changes from 35.3 to 45.71 average accuracy. Conflicting Qwen-7B/14B labels between v2's prose and tables prevent confident matching of some Qwen results.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the CKA/SVD alignment derivation apart from notation. V2 adds a limited computational-cost analysis in Section 3 and Appendix D.6, deriving dense versus selective reconstruction FLOPs, factor and landmark storage, and GPU versus total-memory compression ratios.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes compression improvements over MiniCache and compatibility with MLA. V2 expands the central contribution to selective reconstruction, multi-turn robustness, and practical latency reduction, claiming up to 4.23× generation throughput and approximately 30% higher throughput than ShadowKV. Its conclusion also broadens comparative accuracy claims to quantization and token-eviction methods.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's prospective system discussion with explanations of dense reconstruction's compute bottleneck, offloading's PCIe limits, and SR's efficiency tradeoffs. It adds interpretations of multi-turn eviction failures and window-size saturation. Long generation becomes an explicit unresolved limitation, whereas v1 suggested periodically recompressing generated tokens.

D1.justification: V2 adds SR pseudocode and implementation details, baseline implementation sources, hardware information, and a custom randomized SVD kernel using 16-bit operations and shifted Cholesky QR. The code URL remains unchanged. V1's explicit MLA-specific treatment of latent and decoupled RoPE caches is omitted, and v2's prefill hardware attribution conflicts between prose and table captions.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around dynamic token selection and offloading, explicitly acknowledging ShadowKV's selective reconstruction and presenting xKV as its cross-layer, fully GPU-resident extension. It adds references including Quest, MInference, SCBench, and KVzip, broadening the discussion beyond v1's low-rank and inter-layer emphasis.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, analysis, and methodology are extensively rewritten, with a new contribution list and revised terminology. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, accuracy and efficiency receive separate sections, and the original MLA evaluation and key/value ablation move into appendices. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, replaces the opening performance chart with a strategy-comparison schematic, and redraws the inference diagram to include SR. It adds multi-turn, efficiency, and broader CKA figures, expanded tables, and algorithm boxes. The MLA chart is relocated and revised; the key/value ablation plot is retained in the appendix.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly lacked an end-to-end system demonstration. V2 addresses that important gap with an implemented SR pipeline and measured latency/throughput comparisons in Section 5, while broader baselines and multi-turn tests strengthen practical validation. Conflicting Qwen labels and prefill figures, plus superiority claims broader than Tables 1 and 6 support, weaken reporting precision. Nevertheless, resolving the system-validation gap provides a substantial net improvement.
